title: Intro to BREAD
text: Many methylation studies purely discovery-oriented. Instead asking “CpGs significant genome-wide?”, question often: PRC2 target regions hypermethylated old vs. young samples? bivalent promoters coherently lose methylation treatment? Among predefined chromatin classes (LADs, PMDs, CGIs, …), show strong directional evidence biologically meaningful effect size? Existing tooling strong genome-wide hypothesis testing, answering questions directly benefits : region-centric inference (one answer per region, per CpG), threshold-based decisions biologically meaningful effect sizes, posterior probabilities rather p-values, borrowing strength across probes inside region. BREAD provides minimal, interpretable Bayesian workflow exactly targeted questions, built around SummarizedExperiment GRanges.

title: Intro to BREAD
code: library(BREAD) library(SummarizedExperiment) library(GenomicRanges) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork)

what: Build a toy young-vs-old methylation experiment
title: Intro to BREAD
text: simulate 60 CpG probes chromosome 1 spaced every 1 kb, across 16 samples (8 young, 8 old). define five regions interest — mix PRC-like, CGI-like, LAD-like feature classes — inject strong hyper hypo signal can see BREAD recover .
code: n_probes  <- 60L n_samples <- 16L  # Probe-level GRanges (rowRanges of the SE) probes <- GRanges(   seqnames = "chr1",   ranges   = IRanges(start = seq(1L, by = 1000L, length.out = n_probes),                      width = 1L) ) names(probes) <- sprintf("cg%04d", seq_len(n_probes))  # Sample metadata coldata <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(   group = factor(rep(c("young", "old"), each = n_samples / 2),                  levels = c("young", "old")),   sex   = factor(rep(c("F", "M"), length.out = n_samples)),   row.names = sprintf("S%02d", seq_len(n_samples)) )  # Baseline M-values: noise centered at 0 X <- matrix(   rnorm(n_probes * n_samples, mean = 0, sd = 0.3),   nrow = n_probes,   dimnames = list(names(probes), rownames(coldata)) )  # Regions we care about (biologically predefined sets) regions <- GRanges(   seqnames = "chr1",   ranges   = IRanges(     start = c(    1L, 10001L, 20001L, 30001L, 45001L),     end   = c(10000L, 19000L, 28000L, 40000L, 55000L)   ),   feature_class = c("PRC", "CGI", "LAD", "PRC", "LAD") ) names(regions) <- c("PRC_early", "CGI_island", "LAD_chr1q",                     "PRC_mid",   "LAD_distal")  # Inject signal: in "old" samples, PRC_early gains ~1 M-value, LAD_chr1q loses ~1. # CGI_island, PRC_mid, LAD_distal are left at baseline (should come out inconclusive). old_mask <- coldata$group == "old" probe_in <- function(gr) which(IRanges::overlapsAny(probes, gr)) X[probe_in(regions["PRC_early"]), old_mask] <-   X[probe_in(regions["PRC_early"]), old_mask] + 1.0 X[probe_in(regions["LAD_chr1q"]), old_mask] <-   X[probe_in(regions["LAD_chr1q"]), old_mask] - 1.0  se <- SummarizedExperiment(   assays    = list(M = X),   rowRanges = probes,   colData   = coldata ) se #> class: RangedSummarizedExperiment  #> dim: 60 16  #> metadata(0): #> assays(1): M #> rownames(60): cg0001 cg0002 ... cg0059 cg0060 #> rowData names(0): #> colnames(16): S01 S02 ... S15 S16 #> colData names(2): group sex

title: Intro to BREAD
text: One call maps probes regions, summarizes per sample, fits Bayesian region-level model, classifies region hyper, hypo, inconclusive. <BreadFit> printout summarizes pipeline: mode, backend, contrast, thresholds, many supplied regions survived min_probes, distribution classifications.
code: fit <- fit_bread(   se,   features    = regions,   design      = ~ group + sex,   contrast    = "groupold",   assay_name  = "M",   input_scale = "M",   delta       = 0.10,   prob_cutoff = 0.95,   min_probes  = 3L,   summary_fun = "mean",   feature_class_col = "feature_class" ) fit #> <BreadFit> #>   mode       : summary  #>   backend    : conjugate  #>   input_scale: M  #>   assay      : M  #>   contrast   : groupold  #>   delta      : 0.1  #>   prob_cutoff: 0.95  #>   n_regions  : 5 (of  5  input) #>   classifications: #>     hypermethylated  1 #>     hypomethylated   1 #>     inconclusive     3

what: What the model is doing (under the hood)
title: Intro to BREAD
text: region r, BREAD (v1) fits conjugate Normal–Inverse-Gamma regression summarized region values: yir∼𝒩(Xiβr,σr2),βr∣σr2∼𝒩(μ0,σr2Λ0−1),σr2∼Inv-Gamma(a0,b0). y_{ir} \sim \mathcal{N}\bigl(X_i \beta_r,\ \sigma_r^2\bigr),\quad \beta_r \mid \sigma_r^2 \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_0,\ \sigma_r^2 \Lambda_0^{-1}),\quad \sigma_r^2 \sim \text{Inv-Gamma}(a_0, b_0). posterior closed form. update, marginal posterior single coefficient location-scale Student-t: βr,k∣y∼t2an(μn,k,bnan[Λn−1]kk), \beta_{r,k} \mid y \sim t_{2 a_n}\!\left(\mu_{n,k},\ \tfrac{b_n}{a_n} [\Lambda_n^{-1}]_{kk}\right), BREAD uses compute posterior probabilities directly via pt() / qt() — MCMC. keeps v1 fast, deterministic, trivially installable. Partial pooling across regions MCMC-backed priors planned hierarchical mode v2. Posterior probabilities drive classification: P(βr,k>δ∣y)P(\beta_{r,k} > \delta \mid y) → ≥\geprob_cutoff, classify hypermethylated P(βr,k<−δ∣y)P(\beta_{r,k} < -\delta \mid y) → ≥\geprob_cutoff, classify hypomethylated otherwise inconclusive. can customize prior bread_prior():
code: # A slightly tighter prior on coefficients prior <- bread_prior(lambda0 = 0.1, a0 = 1, b0 = 1) fit2  <- fit_bread(se, regions, ~ group, "groupold", prior = prior,                    feature_class_col = "feature_class") classifications(fit2) #>         PRC_early        CGI_island         LAD_chr1q           PRC_mid  #> "hypermethylated"    "inconclusive"  "hypomethylated"    "inconclusive"  #>        LAD_distal  #>    "inconclusive"

title: BREAD on real EPICv2 data: vitamin C in serially passaged fibroblasts
text: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) cofactor TET dioxygenases, oxidize 5mC → 5hmC → 5fC → 5caC drive active DNA demethylation. TET activity thought protect CpG islands aberrant age-associated hypermethylation. serially passaged human fibroblasts, two CpG sets consistently change: PRC-CGI (Polycomb-marked CpG islands, H3K27me3 ∩ CGI) gain methylation passage number; PMD-soloWCGW (late-replicating solo-WCGW CpGs within partially methylated domains) lose methylation passage number. question experiment asks: VitC supplementation attenuate either signal? conventional probe-level DMP pipeline reports significant CpGs; BREAD asks complementary, region-centric question directly: predefined feature region, posterior probability methylation effect exceeds biologically meaningful threshold?

title: BREAD on real EPICv2 data: vitamin C in serially passaged fibroblasts
text: BREAD ships small (~0.5 MB) subset real EPICv2 experiment lab — 8 arrays AG06561 fetal skin fibroblasts across 2 × 2 design (condition × passage × 2 technical replicates). data-raw builder data-raw/make_vitc_extdata.R (source repository). Five feature classes, 100 regions , autosomes, region spanning ≥ 3 EPICv2 probes ±2 kb merge. reg$feature_class drive plot_feature_set() stratification .
code: library(BREAD) library(SummarizedExperiment) library(GenomicRanges) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork)  se  <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "vitc_ag06561.rds", package = "BREAD")) reg <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "vitc_regions.rds", package = "BREAD")) se #> class: RangedSummarizedExperiment  #> dim: 6716 8  #> metadata(0): #> assays(1): betas #> rownames(6716): cg00003513 cg00004633 ... cg27639620 cg27642771 #> rowData names(7): Probe_ID CpG_Island ... H3K27AC H3K4ME3 #> colnames(8): 209725120091_R01C01 209725120091_R02C01 ... #>   209725120091_R07C01 209725120091_R08C01 #> colData names(16): total_num batch_num ... sample_label group as.data.frame(colData(se)[, c("condition", "passage", "replicate")]) #>                     condition passage replicate #> 209725120091_R01C01      ctrl   early         1 #> 209725120091_R02C01      ctrl    late         1 #> 209725120091_R03C01      ctrl   early         2 #> 209725120091_R04C01      ctrl    late         2 #> 209725120091_R05C01      aa57   early         1 #> 209725120091_R06C01      aa57    late         1 #> 209725120091_R07C01      aa57   early         2 #> 209725120091_R08C01      aa57    late         2 length(reg); table(reg$feature_class) #> [1] 500 #>  #> Active_enhancer Active_promoter        Bivalent    PMD_soloWCGW         PRC_CGI  #>             100             100             100             100             100

title: Fit a Bayesian region-specific methylation model — fit_bread
text: Main user-facing entry point. Given SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment methylation assay GenomicRanges::GRanges predefined regions, BREAD maps probes regions, summarizes per sample, fits Bayesian region-level models produce posterior probabilities directional methylation change contrast interest. Regions classified hypermethylated, hypomethylated, inconclusive.

title: Fit a Bayesian region-specific methylation model — fit_bread
text: se SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment methylation assay. features GenomicRanges::GRanges user-defined regions. design one-sided formula giving model design, e.g. ~ group + sex. contrast Character coefficient name interest. NULL (default), first non-intercept coefficient used message emitted. assay_name Assay name se. Default "M". input_scale "M" "Beta". Beta inputs converted M internally. mode "summary" (v1) "hierarchical" (planned). summary_fun Region summary: "mean" (default), "median", "weighted_mean", "pc1". delta Effect-size threshold M-value scale. Default 0.10. prob_cutoff Posterior probability cutoff classification. Default 0.95. min_probes Minimum probes per region. Default 3. feature_class_col Column mcols(features) giving feature class (reserved class-level pooling M3). backend One "conjugate" (default, v1), "brms", "cmdstanr". prior bread_prior() object NULL defaults. iter, chains, cores, seed MCMC settings. Reserved "brms" / "cmdstanr" backends; ignored "conjugate".

title: Fit BREAD summary-mode Bayesian model — fit_bread_summary
text: list : fits: per-region list list(mu_n, Lambda_n_inv, a_n, b_n, n, error) design_matrix: model matrix X actually used coef_names: coefficient names contrast, contrast_idx: contrast name column index X region_ids: rownames region_mat prior: prior applied (mu0/Lambda0 filled )

title: Fit BREAD summary-mode Bayesian model — fit_bread_summary
text: region r sample : $$y_{ir} \sim \mathcal{N}(X_i \beta_r,\, \sigma_r^2),$$ $$\beta_r \mid \sigma_r^2 \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_0,\, \sigma_r^2 \Lambda_0^{-1}),$$ $$\sigma_r^2 \sim \mathrm{Inv\text{-}Gamma}(a_0, b_0).$$ Posterior: $$\Lambda_n = X^\top X + \Lambda_0,\quad \mu_n = \Lambda_n^{-1}(X^\top y + \Lambda_0 \mu_0),$$ $$a_n = a_0 + n/2,\quad b_n = b_0 + \tfrac{1}{2}(y^\top y + \mu_0^\top \Lambda_0 \mu_0 - \mu_n^\top \Lambda_n \mu_n).$$

title: Summarize probe-level methylation into region-level values — summarize_features
text: "mean" (default): arithmetic mean probes per region per sample. "median": per-sample median across probes region. "weighted_mean": inverse-variance weighting, probe's weight 1 / max(var_across_samples, 1e-6). Probes zero variance receive minimum-variance weight; probes zero variance, weights fall back uniform (reducing plain mean). "pc1": first principal component probes (SVD row-centering). Returned scores sign-aligned correlate positively per-sample mean across probes. Scale abstract — delta loses M-value interpretation "pc1".
